summary: Sketch mode shows the part behind the sketch, and can cut it at the sketch plane. While a sketch is open, the 3D view stays under the sketch canvas instead of being hidden, drawn through an orthographic camera that looks along the sketch plane's normal with the sketch's V axis up and the canvas's view box as its frustum, so every point of the part lands on the pixel of the matching sketch point and the sketch's pan and zoom move both together. Solids, the other sketches and curves are drawn; the open sketch draws itself, and planes, the grid, the axes and pick highlights stay out of the way. The View drawer below the dock gains 3D background, with Dimmed, the default, Normal and Hidden, and Cut part by sketch plane. Dimmed blends every drawn colour 62% toward the view's background gradient at that pixel and keeps depth, so the part reads as 3D and the open sketch stays dominant; Normal draws the part as in the 3D view; Hidden draws nothing behind the sketch, as before. The cut clips away everything on the viewer's side of the sketch plane, with a small tolerance that keeps faces lying on the plane, on the solids, their edges and the other sketches, without caps. The choices are remembered on the device for the next sketch and are not part of the document. The view behind the sketch draws only when the sketch view pans, zooms or resizes, or when the model, its lines or the choices change: hovering, dragging or drawing in the sketch draws no 3D frame. The sketch canvas keeps every pointer, focus and keyboard input, and nothing in 3D can be picked during sketch mode. Leaving the sketch returns the model camera exactly as it was, and shows the planes and lines the sketch left out again without rebuilding them.
warning: No breaking change for CAD files, installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions or controller output. Potentially breaking for automation that inspects the page in sketch mode: the 3D viewport element stays in the page behind the sketch canvas, as div.cad-viewport.is-sketch-background with aria-hidden="true", pointer-events none and its canvas out of the tab order, where it was a hidden element; its graphics host carries data-cad-frames-drawn, a count of frames drawn. Selectors that expect no visible .cad-viewport or WebGL canvas during sketch mode, or that count canvas elements, must allow for it. Screenshots of sketch mode now show the part behind the sketch, dimmed by default; captures through cad_capture_preview still show only the sketch. The View drawer in sketch mode gains a 3D background select and a Cut part by sketch plane check box, so automation that counts its controls or tab stops must allow for them. Device preferences under wire-edm:cad-preferences:v1 gain an optional sketchView field; releases 0.0.786 and earlier ignore it and drop it when they next write the preferences, which returns the choices to Dimmed and uncut.

checklist.schema: No CAD document, sketch, UPID, post, machine package, saved revision, storage, journal or worker protocol change. Device preferences (localStorage wire-edm:cad-preferences:v1) gain an optional sketchView: {background: 'normal' | 'dimmed' | 'hidden', cutBySketchPlane: boolean}; a value this release cannot read is ignored and the other preferences stay in force, and stored bytes are never rewritten except by an explicit choice. The view state is modelled in src/features/cad/view/cadViewState.ts as a part or sketch context with background, cut and a pick scope that is only 'sketch' for now, so a later section view and selection filter extend it. Post engine API remains 1 and saved-job engine remains 3.
checklist.events: No execution event or input-version behavior change. The sketch canvas publishes its view box through a camera link outside React whenever the view frame changes; the link drops a view equal to the last one, and the viewport draws at most one frame per animation frame when a new view arrives. A frame is drawn behind the sketch only for a new view, a changed model, changed lines behind the sketch, a resize or a changed choice; a new document version that leaves the lines the same, as a sketch edit does, draws nothing. The viewport behind the sketch publishes no viewport controls, so WebMCP viewport commands and captures in sketch mode reach the sketch canvas as before. The lines the open sketch leaves out of its background, the planes and its own lines, are kept out of the scene with their buffers and shader programs while it is open, so leaving the sketch shows them again without rebuilding them; a line changed meanwhile is rebuilt, as before. A region pick shows the 3D view itself, as before; a sketch reference pick or a profile copy preview, which draw their own sketch surface, still hide the part behind it, as before.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change, and no WebMCP tool added, removed or changed. The View drawer in sketch mode adds 3D background (Normal, Dimmed, Hidden) and Cut part by sketch plane, which is disabled while the background is Hidden, with help that says picks reach only the open sketch and that the choices stay on this device. A Pick only in current sketch control is left out: a disabled check box cannot take focus, so its help would be unreachable, and the pick scope is stated in the help instead. The exact section outline from the solid kernel is left out: the kernel section supports principal planes only and would need a new worker request per build and plane, which is more risk than this change carries; the cut shows the section edge where the clipped faces end. The shared UI components and theme are unchanged.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change. The sketch view choices live only in the device preference key above, in browser local storage, and are not saved in documents, the browser cache workbench or the folder adapter.
checklist.verification: New unit suites: cadViewState (reducer, remembered choices, reading stored choices field by field), cadSketchCamera (every sketch point on its canvas pixel within 0.001 px at several zooms and pans on principal, offset, datum and flipped planes; view direction, up and depth range; the cut for both senses of the normal; the camera link drops equal views), cadSketchBackgroundStyle (the dim blend in lit, basic and dashed shaders, one shared amount and one program for Normal and Dimmed, and reuse of unchanged background references), cadPreferences (sketchView stored with the other preferences; an unreadable value ignored without dropping the rest). CadViewport: drawing only through the sketch camera and only for a new view, model, lines or choice, one frame per pan or zoom step, none for a repeated view or Hidden, the dim and cut uniforms and planes with local clipping on, the model camera restored exactly; no frame for a new document version with the same lines; lines left out of the background kept aside and shown again unrebuilt, a line edited meanwhile replaced, and set-aside lines disposed with the view. CadSketchViewModes: the workbench shows the part dimmed, switches Normal, Hidden and the cut from the View drawer and stores them, opens the next sketch with them; hover, a box drag, Line hover and a Line drag that commits publish no view and hand the viewport nothing new, and one wheel step publishes one view. Chromium spec cad-sketch-view-modes: pixel probes at sketch coordinates for Normal, Dimmed (0.15 to 0.6 of Normal) and Hidden, the cut in Normal and Dimmed removing a raised block and keeping the plate, no 3D frame during hover, a box drag or Line hover and exactly one per wheel step, the background aria-hidden, without pointer events and out of the tab order, and the model camera and plane labels restored after finishing. Mutations, each caught: dropping the on-demand guard in the viewport (unit frame-count tests; the spec never settles), publishing every canvas render (link, viewport and workbench tests; the spec sees frames during hover), breaking the camera sync (pixel test, viewport test; the spec loses the block in Normal), dropping the material clipping planes or turning local clipping off (viewport tests; the spec still sees the block with the cut), disposing instead of setting aside (the set-aside test). Checks: full Vitest 6682 of 6683 passed, the one failure a 5 s timeout in the unrelated path editor test editorPathNativeDraft, which passed 105 of 105 alone; npm run build including the e2e type-check and the docs check; oxlint with zero findings; npm run ui:check; check-release against origin/main fails only because previousVersion 0.0.786 is one above main's 0.0.785. Chromium specs run singly with two workers: cad-sketch-view-modes 1, cad-sketch-constraints 28, cad-sketch-relation-glyphs 7, cad-sketch-dimension-selection 4, cad-sketch-selectable-axes 1, cad-sketch-placement 1, cad-sketch-editing 2, cad-sketch-persistent-reference 1, cad-sketch-profile-copy 1, cad-sketch-context-editing 1, cad-region-workflow 1, cad-workflow 32 and cad-kernel 2, all passed. Measurements at 4x CPU in Chromium with SwiftShader on 60 constrained rectangles, recorded in docs/maintainers/cad-performance.md: no 3D frame during any hover; Select hover P50 21.7 ms Dimmed and 22.3 ms Hidden; Line hover P50 about 3 ms higher in Dimmed (30.5 against 27.5 ms) in quiet sessions, the cost of compositing the WebGL layer, and within noise on a loaded machine; exit from Dimmed 51 ms against 55 ms in Hidden after keeping the left-out lines aside, where it was 89 against 40 ms before; heap, DOM nodes, listeners and canvases unchanged over 10 enter and exit cycles.

publicNotes.summary: The part stays visible behind a sketch, and can be cut at the sketch plane.
changes: While you edit a sketch, the part and the other sketches stay visible behind it, lined up with the sketch, and pan and zoom with it.
Open View below the dock to set 3D background to Dimmed, the default, Normal or Hidden.
Cut part by sketch plane removes everything on your side of the sketch plane, so you see the part where the sketch lies.
Your choices are remembered in this browser for the next sketch. Clicks and drags still reach only the sketch, and leaving the sketch returns the 3D view as you left it.
publicNotes.compatibility: No file, schema or tool change. Installed machine packages, posts, saved revisions and controller output are unchanged.
publicNotes.action: No action is needed. Automation that inspects sketch mode must allow for the 3D view element behind the sketch canvas and the two new View controls.
